_meta.label: SYNTHETIC. Illustrative parameters for a teaching example. Not ADIC data and not a forecast.
_meta.version: 2 (2026-10-19). Applies the corrections in verify_math.md and verify_finance.md; RESULTS.md section 10 lists every change and its reason.
_meta.units: Money in $bn. Rates are annual decimals (0.07 = 7%). Stages are years: decisions at t = 0, 1, 2; t = 3 is the horizon.
_meta.how_to_change: Edit a 'value' and re-run tree_demo.py. Every number the program uses is in this file, including the reporting thresholds in 'settings'. Only the solver's own settings (dual simplex, tolerances, objective scaling) are in the script.
_meta.regime_codes: N = normal; D = PE distribution drought; C = crisis with an oil shock (oil weak, so the owner draws more).

start_regime.rationale: Today reads as a PE distribution drought; the toy treats the 0.87 drought posterior as being in D.
start_regime.source: research/00_SYNTHESIS.md (initial state: exit window drought 0.87, Oct 2026); research/addenda/gap_04.md

transition_matrix.unit: probability of next year's regime given this year's (rows sum to 1)
transition_matrix.rationale: Persistent regimes. D to C = 15% sits inside the research's 13-35% range for P(stress within 12 months). C persists 30%: a mean crisis spell of 1/(1 - 0.30) = 1.4 years (17 months), inside the research's 6-18-month crisis dwell. v1 used 40% (20 months); RESULTS.md section 7 shows it as a sensitivity.
transition_matrix.source: research/00_RESEARCH_SUFFICIENCY.md row 11 (P(stress within 12 months) 13-35%); research crisis dwell 6-18 months (verify_finance.md L1)

decision_stages.rationale: Decisions at t = 0, 1, 2; leaves at t = 3. 1 + 3 + 9 + 27 = 40 nodes. RESULTS.md section 6 re-solves the same program with 2 and 4 years to show which results depend on where the tree stops.

cash_hqla.rationale: Treasury cash + IG held by Corporate Finance (8.5% of NAV), tracked separately from the risky liquid book.

liquid_book.rationale: Public Markets: hedge funds 20 + long-only 36. With the 15 of cash this is the $71bn liquid book.

pe_book_nav.rationale: PE-like book: PE funds 34 + Secondaries 14 + Co-investment 18 (the red-tier groups).

pe_unfunded.rationale: Unfunded commitments of the PE-like book; inside the task's 16-20 range (census v1.1 PE figure $16.4bn plus Secondaries deferred payments and co-investment).

yield_book_nav.rationale: Private Credit 14 + Capital Solutions 8 + Real Assets 18. Pays cash yield; held (no decision) in this toy.

cash_rate.rationale: Cash/HQLA and posted margin earn SOFR; also the base rate of every loan.

return_model.rationale: Regimes decide which year happens (cash flows, bids, facility availability, the owner's draw) and the shape of the year, but give the program nothing to time: next year's expected return and volatility are the same from every regime. The script maps the year's return to R[i][j] = mean + (sd*/sd_i)(r_j - m_i), with m_i and sd_i the mean and volatility of r over row i of the transition matrix and sd* the start regime's (RESULTS.md section 9 prints the matrix; nothing in it is set by hand). So a crisis after a calm year is a deeper loss than a crisis after a crisis. In v1, regimes predicted the mean (10.1% next year from N, 6.65% from C), so the program timed the market and the IC range did the work of stopping it. Equal means alone are not enough: the crisis row's higher volatility still made the program sell its liquid book down in crisis years (checked; RESULTS.md section 7, 'means only').
return_model.source: verify_finance.md M2 and H3; research (CAPE timing R^2 -5% to -56% out of sample); design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.11 (CAPE and mean-reversion timing excluded)

liquid_volatility.unit: volatility of next year's liquid return from every regime; null = the start regime's (9.5%)
liquid_volatility.rationale: Keeps year 1 from today's drought exactly as the regime returns below say (shifted by +0.3pp to the CMA mean).

pe_volatility.unit: volatility of next year's reported PE NAV return from every regime; null = the start regime's (7.6%)
pe_volatility.rationale: Same convention as the liquid book.

liquid_return.unit: total return in the year by that year's regime, before the return model's mapping
liquid_return.rationale: Shape of the year for the blended long-only + hedge-fund book. C is a 2022-like year for this blend (long-only about -18%, hedge funds about -4%).

liquid_expected_return.unit: expected total return next year, from every regime
liquid_expected_return.rationale: Blend of the long-only and hedge-fund CMAs (36 x 7.5% + 20 x 6.7%) / 56.
liquid_expected_return.source: research CMAs (ACWI 7.5%, hedge funds 6.7%), as cited in verify_finance.md section 6

pe_nav_return.unit: reported NAV total return in the year (value created, before distributions), before the return model's mapping
pe_nav_return.rationale: Reported NAVs are smoothed, so the crisis loss is smaller than in public markets. Terminal wealth uses economic value instead (terminal.pe_value_per_nav).

pe_expected_return.unit: expected reported-NAV return next year, from every regime
pe_expected_return.source: research CMA (PE 9.6%), as cited in verify_finance.md section 6

pe_distribution_rate.unit: share of opening PE NAV paid out as cash in the year
pe_distribution_rate.source: research/00_SYNTHESIS.md data table (MSCI Private Capital: 17-24% 2017-20, 27% 2021, 9-11% 2022-25, 9% H1-26)

pe_call_rate.unit: share of opening unfunded called in the year
pe_call_rate.rationale: 28% of unfunded is the research base rate; calls rise in a crisis (the T4' replica scales calls up to 1.38x).
pe_call_rate.source: research/00_SYNTHESIS.md (calls at 28% of unfunded; T4' calls x1.38)

yield_cash_rate.unit: cash yield paid in the year, share of opening yield-book NAV
yield_cash_rate.rationale: Blend of private credit (about 10% cash), capital solutions (about 7%) and real-asset income; lower in a crisis (defaults, PIK toggles).
yield_cash_rate.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.9 conventions (credit cash: Private Credit 10%, Capital Solutions 7%)

yield_nav_return.unit: NAV change in the year, excluding the cash yield
yield_nav_return.rationale: Credit losses and real-asset write-downs in a crisis (total return in C is -1% with the 5% cash yield). The yield book has no decisions, so its regime pattern creates no timing.

owner_draw_rate.unit: share of opening-of-year NAV the owner calls in the year (exogenous, must be paid)
owner_draw_rate.rationale: The owner sets 5-10% of NAV, higher when oil is weak. The draw follows oil, not PE exits, so N and D draw the same: 5.8% x $177bn = $10.3bn, inside the research's 12-month estimate of $9.9-10.8bn. C carries an oil shock to about $45 Brent: 7.5% on the research's line (5% at $67 or more, 10% at $23 or less). The 10% cap needs Brent below about $23, which the research puts at about 1.2% for 2027, far below C's 15%; RESULTS.md section 7 shows a 10% crisis draw and v1's 6 / 7.5 / 10% as sensitivities.
owner_draw_rate.source: user (2026-10-18): 5-10% of NAV, higher when oil is weak; research/00_SYNTHESIS.md (draw at the 5% floor above about $67 Brent, 10% cap below about $23; 12-month draw $9.9-10.8bn; P(2027 draw >= 9.5%) about 1.2%); verify_finance.md M3

liquid_trade_cost.rationale: Blended long-only impact and hedge-fund redemption friction.
liquid_trade_cost.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.8 (long-only: sale at impact cost); SYNTHETIC

pe_secondary_discount.unit: discount to reported NAV on a SELL of PE interests, by the regime at the sale
pe_secondary_discount.rationale: Normal LP-led bids 91-94% of NAV; drought bids weaker; crisis fire sale near the H2-2008 average high bid of 61% of NAV. 35% is a stress case for fund interests (the research's market-adjusted crisis bids are about 83.5%); RESULTS.md section 7 shows 25%.
pe_secondary_discount.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.8 (buyout 0.91-0.94; crisis residual 0.80-0.84); research/dossiers/05_secondaries_navfin.md (H2-2008 high bids 61% of NAV)

unfunded_assumed_per_nav_sold.unit: $ of unfunded the buyer takes over per $ of NAV sold
unfunded_assumed_per_nav_sold.rationale: Pro-rata sale at today's ratio U/NAV = 18/66, held fixed so the program stays linear.
unfunded_assumed_per_nav_sold.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.4 (kappa_U; 0.53 for the PE-funds bucket under census v1.0)

nav_loan_ltv_cap.unit: maximum NAV-loan balance as a share of the pledge pool at the node
nav_loan_ltv_cap.rationale: REFINANCE capacity; lenders cut LTV in stress, which forces a paydown, including at the horizon.
nav_loan_ltv_cap.source: research/00_SYNTHESIS.md (NAV facility LTV 10-20%, stress -5 to -10pp); design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.9 (5% stressed LTV)

nav_loan_pledge_pool_frac.unit: share of private NAV (PE-like book + yield book) that may be pledged
nav_loan_pledge_pool_frac.rationale: The architecture caps private pledges at 20% of private NAV, so capacity is 10% x 20% x $106bn = $2.1bn today and $1.1bn at the 5% stressed LTV. v1 pledged the whole PE book ($6.6bn), 2.5-3 times the cap; RESULTS.md section 7 shows it as a sensitivity.
nav_loan_pledge_pool_frac.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md sections 4.8 (pledge cap about $2.1bn at 10% LTV, $1.1bn credited at 5%) and 4.10 (private pledges <= 20% of private NAV); verify_finance.md M4

nav_loan_pledge_pool_includes_yield_book.unit: true: the pool is a share of PE-like + yield-book NAV; false: of the PE-like book only
nav_loan_pledge_pool_includes_yield_book.rationale: Private NAV in the architecture includes Private Credit, Capital Solutions and Real Assets.

nav_loan_spread.unit: spread over SOFR, set by the regime when the balance is carried into the next year
nav_loan_spread.rationale: SOFR + 300bp base, wider in a drought, +140bp in stress.

revolver_limit.rationale: Committed revolver (Corporate Finance). Present only in the with_revolver case (consent scenario R1: a signed facility).
revolver_limit.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.5 (R1: committed revolver up to $15bn)

revolver_availability.unit: share of the limit that may be outstanding at the node
revolver_availability.rationale: Availability 100 / 100 / 50% by regime; in C a balance above 50% must be repaid, including at the horizon.
revolver_availability.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.4 H2 (facility availability by regime 100/100/50%)

revolver_drawn_spread.unit: spread over SOFR on drawn balances

revolver_undrawn_fee.unit: per year on the undrawn limit
revolver_undrawn_fee.rationale: Commitment fee: the cost of having the facility.

lever_financing_spread.unit: spread over SOFR embedded in synthetic exposure (futures or TRS), locked by the regime when the position is put on
lever_financing_spread.rationale: LEVER and P2S hold liquid-book exposure synthetically; the position earns the liquid return minus SOFR minus this spread. About 30bp on average, 81bp at the June-2026 roll (a drought-like market), 175bp in stress. v1 used a flat 60bp.
lever_financing_spread.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.10 (futures financing about 30bp average, 81bp at the June-2026 roll, 175bp stress); verify_finance.md L7

lever_initial_margin.unit: initial margin posted in cash per $ of synthetic notional, by regime at the node
lever_initial_margin.rationale: Posted margin is still ADIC's asset but is encumbered, so it does not count toward the cash floor or target; IM roughly doubles in stress.
lever_initial_margin.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.9 conventions (IM 4% to 10% on the shock)

no_liquid_purchases_in_regimes.unit: regimes in which the program may not buy liquid-book assets (decision nodes and t = 3)
no_liquid_purchases_in_regimes.rationale: The CFP Red playbook draws lines, uses P2S and sells long-only; it does not add risk. Without this rule a crisis year could borrow on the revolver to buy equities (checked in the 4-year tree), which is LEVER while the fund is in CFP Red (verify_finance.md H6: block LEVER and borrowed purchases below Amber). The crisis regime stands in for event-Red, because the stage itself depends on the decision and an LP cannot condition on it.
no_liquid_purchases_in_regimes.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.9 (CFP stages and playbooks); verify_finance.md H6

synthetic_notional_cap.unit: $bn of synthetic liquid-book notional the program may hold
synthetic_notional_cap.rationale: Budget for new synthetic beta on top of the overlay's existing book. P2S is a REFINANCE of the liquid book, so without a budget it would be an unlimited cheap source of cash.
synthetic_notional_cap.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.8 (P2S as REFINANCE; P2S cap in H2) and section 4.9 conventions ($10bn synthetic beta already in the overlay)

synthetic_use.unit: 'p2s_only': synthetic exposure only replaces physical sold (P2S, a REFINANCE); 'p2s_and_lever': synthetic beta may also be added (LEVER)
synthetic_use.rationale: The architecture's doctrine: for the aggregate book the use's alpha* is r_f - c < 0, so leverage is a liquidity and implementation tool, not a route to 10%. The liquid book here is beta with no alpha, so adding it with borrowed or synthetic money cannot pass the LEVER test. P2S and unwinds are separate columns, so the program cannot dress a LEVER up as a P2S. A borrowed purchase of physical assets is still possible and is labelled LEVER; the own-liquidity target makes it costly. RESULTS.md section 7 shows the result with synthetic LEVER allowed.
synthetic_use.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md sections 4.8 (LEVER test: alpha* - risk charge > all-in financing cost) and 4.10 (doctrine); verify_finance.md H5 and H6

pacing_plan.unit: $bn of new PE commitments planned each year
pacing_plan.rationale: Roughly the PE-like book's steady-state pace (5 / 0.30 call rate = about 17 of unfunded, close to today's 18).
pacing_plan.source: task; research/groups/01_GROUPS_SYNTHESIS.md (sealed pace $5.34bn a year, census v1.1)

pacing_core_sleeve.unit: share of the year's plan that cannot be cut (protected core sleeve)
pacing_core_sleeve.rationale: The pacing corridor in Amber is 0.25-0.5 x plan with a protected core sleeve of at least 25% of plan, so a node can cut at most 75% of its plan. v1 allowed cutting 100%.
pacing_core_sleeve.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md sections 4.8 and 6.5 (corridor Green 0.75-1.25x, Amber 0.25-0.5x with a protected core sleeve >= 25% of plan); verify_finance.md M6

pacing_cut_cost.unit: $ of franchise value lost per $ of commitments cut (non-cash, charged to terminal wealth)
pacing_cut_cost.rationale: c^PACE: forgone net alpha 1.35c + GP access (kappa_GP) 5.12c + lost co-investment flow 2.12c per $ forgone.
pacing_cut_cost.source: research/groups/01_GROUPS_SYNTHESIS.md section 3.1 (c^PACE about 8.6c in M1; 5.6-12.3c across models)

new_commitment_first_year_call_rate.unit: share of a year's new commitments called in that same year
new_commitment_first_year_call_rate.rationale: A cut earns no liquidity credit for two quarters, and commitments signed through the year are first called the following year; so a cut decided at node t lowers calls from year t+2 on.
new_commitment_first_year_call_rate.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.9 conventions (a cut earns no liquidity credit for 2 quarters, S-ADR-20)

cash_floor_frac.unit: unencumbered cash/HQLA as a share of NAV, after paying the owner draw (hard, every node including t = 3)
cash_floor_frac.rationale: Tier 1A hard floor (T2 at 4%), net of posted margin.
cash_floor_frac.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.2 (T2 IG + cash 8% elastic / 4% hard)

cash_target_frac.unit: own liquidity as a share of NAV (elastic target, every node including t = 3)
cash_target_frac.rationale: T2's 8% target. It is an appetite row, never hard: the program may go below it and pays the price below for each $ of shortfall.
cash_target_frac.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md sections 4.9 (IG + cash 8% target, elastic, restored within 4 quarters of exiting stress) and 5.5 (appetite rows are never hard); verify_finance.md H6

cash_target_basis.unit: 'net_of_facility_draws': the target counts unencumbered cash less drawn revolver and NAV-loan balances; 'gross': cash only
cash_target_basis.rationale: A buffer funded by the revolver is a used backstop, not a buffer. Counted gross, any target price above the revolver's net carry (85bp drawn less 15bp undrawn) made the program draw the revolver in every year to hold the target, and borrow to buy (checked; RESULTS.md section 7, 'gross target'). The 4% hard floor stays gross, so a drawn facility still keeps the fund alive in stress, and the CFP Treasury / NAV reading stays gross as in the architecture.
cash_target_basis.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.9 (IG + cash target; facilities are a separate rung of the CFP ladder); verify_finance.md H6

cash_target_shortfall_price.unit: $ of terminal wealth per $ of own liquidity below the 8% target, for one year at a node, by the node's regime; 'horizon' applies at t = 3
cash_target_shortfall_price.rationale: The IC's stated appetite price. 2c a year per $ is clearly above the value of one more dollar of liquid exposure in this tree (about 1% a year), so the program restores the target whenever it can instead of treating it as a cheap option. Today's decision and the crisis response are the same for any price from 1% to 3% (checked); below about 1% the program runs today's Treasury below the target to buy equities (RESULTS.md section 7 shows 0.75%, 1% and no price). Zero in a crisis year: the target is elastic in stress and must be restored within 4 quarters of the stress ending, which in annual steps is the next node. At t = 3 every shortfall is priced, because it still has to be restored after the horizon.
cash_target_shortfall_price.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.9 (restored within 4 quarters of exiting stress); appetite price set for this example

liquid_exposure_min_frac.unit: share of NAV; lower edge of the IC range for public-markets exposure (physical + synthetic), elastic
liquid_exposure_min_frac.rationale: IC allocation range of about +/-5pp around today's 31.6% weight, a human-set limit that the program prices. In v1 the edge was hard everywhere and forced PE fire sales while $27bn of equities remained, and later forced PE sales to restore the range (verify_finance.md H3). It is now elastic: below it, each $ costs the price below.
liquid_exposure_min_frac.source: SYNTHETIC governance limit; design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.4 H2 (node limits)

liquid_exposure_min_shortfall_price.unit: $ of terminal wealth per $ of public-markets exposure below the lower edge, for one year at a node, by the node's regime; 'horizon' applies at t = 3
liquid_exposure_min_shortfall_price.rationale: Same price and logic as the cash target. Free in a crisis year, where the CFP Red playbook sells long-only and uses P2S before any red-tier (PE) sale, and priced again once the crisis ends. A priced breach is never worth a PE sale at an 8-35% discount, so the range can no longer force one.
liquid_exposure_min_shortfall_price.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.9 (CFP stages: event-Red playbook 'lines drawn; P2S and long-only sales'; red sales only at Black); verify_finance.md H3

liquid_exposure_min_hard.unit: true makes the lower edge a hard row everywhere (v1)
liquid_exposure_min_hard.rationale: Kept only for the sensitivity that reproduces v1's hard range.

liquid_exposure_max_frac.unit: share of NAV; upper edge of the IC range (every node including t = 3)
liquid_exposure_max_frac.rationale: Upper edge of the same range; also bounds LEVER.

cvar_floor_annual_return.unit: annualized 3-year total return (owner draws counted), or null for no floor
cvar_floor_annual_return.rationale: No downside floor in the main case. v1's -3.9% a year was set just above the unconstrained tail so that it would bind (verify_finance.md M7). The architecture's Tier-1B bands (+1% / 0% / -2%) apply to the CVaR10% of 10-year windows, which a 3-year tree that starts in a drought cannot test, so a 3-year floor would be a new limit that the IC would have to set. RESULTS.md section 7 shows what floors from -6% to -3% a year would do.
cvar_floor_annual_return.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.2 (Tier 1B on forward 10-year windows); verify_finance.md M7

crra_gamma.rationale: Tier 2 growth objective: E[U(W/W0)] with CRRA gamma = 3, never risk-neutral.

n_tangents.rationale: Concave piecewise-linear utility from 10 tangent lines keeps the program an LP. Checked against 48 tangents (RESULTS.md section 11).
n_tangents.source: task (8-10 tangents); the architecture uses 48 at production size

tangent_first_pass_range.unit: W/W0 range for the first pass; the second pass re-places the tangents on the first solve's leaf range
tangent_first_pass_range.rationale: Adaptive placement as in section 5.4 (tangents on the leaf-wealth range of the previous solve).

pe_value_per_nav.unit: terminal value per $ of reported PE NAV, by the regime of the last year
pe_value_per_nav.rationale: Terminal wealth and CVaR use economic value; reported NAV is kept for LTV, bids and the IC range. After a crisis year the reported mark (-10%) lags an economic loss of about -20% (a de-smoothed beta of about 1.3 to the -15% liquid year), so economic NAV is about 90% of the mark. Floored at 1 - crisis discount (0.65), as the architecture requires. v1 valued PE at 100% of the mark in every leaf.
pe_value_per_nav.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.12 (omega_g, floored at 1 - discount); research section 4.2 (risk and value on economic NAV); verify_finance.md M5

unfunded_burden_per_dollar.unit: terminal charge per $ of unfunded commitment left at t = 3
unfunded_burden_per_dollar.rationale: Unfunded commitments are called after the horizon and must be funded with liquidity that costs something. Stated value: about three years of calls at a liquidity premium of about 0.7% a year. The architecture estimates psi_g by regression on simulated paths, which this toy does not have. v1 set psi = 0, which made pacing cuts look worthless; RESULTS.md section 7 shows 0 and 0.10.

distribution_accrual.unit: how owner draws are credited in terminal wealth
distribution_accrual.rationale: Draws paid are added back to terminal wealth, grown at the path's static-allocation return, so the objective and the 10% test count what the owner received and are neutral to payout timing.
distribution_accrual.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md sections 5.2 and 5.4 (W-tilde with distributions accrued at the static-SAA return)

delta_max.unit: a red-tier sale whose bid is below (1 - delta_max) x the normal-regime bid is a red event
delta_max.rationale: Test (iii) of the economic-substance rule. Crisis bids (65% against 92%) fail it; drought bids (85% against 92%) pass it.

normal_regime.unit: regime whose bid is the 'normal bid' in test (iii)

cfp_event_thresholds.unit: lower edges of Green, Amber and Red; below the last value is Black
cfp_event_thresholds.rationale: The two CFP event indicators the toy carries: Treasury / NAV and the physical liquid share. The stage is the worse of the two, read after the node's actions. A PE sale is a red event if the stage is Amber or worse, if Treasury is below the 8% target, or if the bid fails test (iii).
cfp_event_thresholds.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.9 (CFP stages) and section 5.2 (ADR-39 tests (ii) and (iii))

root_red_tier_sell_rule.unit: what happens to a PE SELL at the root
root_red_tier_sell_rule.rationale: If today's event stage is Amber or worse, or if the root's PE sale would be a red event, the root PE SELL is held at zero and priced by a forced re-solve that allows it; the IC sees both. Today's stage is computed from the opening balance sheet (Treasury 8.5%, liquid share 31.6%: Green). The architecture's t0 reading on census v1.0 was Amber; under Amber every root PE sale would be held at zero.
root_red_tier_sell_rule.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md sections 5.2 (ADR-39) and 5.4 (red-tier SELL columns held at zero in Phase II and priced by forced re-solve); verify_finance.md M8

cash_target_frac.rationale: Naive Treasury rule under the same limits as the optimizer: aim for the 8% target by selling liquid assets inside the IC range (whose lower edge is waived in crisis years, as for the optimizer), or sweep surplus cash into liquid up to the upper edge; trim the liquid book to the upper edge when markets push it above; sell PE at the regime discount only if the 4% floor would otherwise fail. It never refinances, borrows, levers, uses P2S or cuts pacing, and it has no look-ahead.
cash_target_frac.source: task (sell liquid first, never refinance or lever)

variant_cash_target_frac.rationale: Same naive rule run at the 4% floor, to separate the cost of a bigger buffer from the value of the other levers.

revolver_first_variant.unit: also run the naive rule with the signed revolver: drawn when the 4% floor would otherwise fail, before any liquid sale below the IC range or PE sale ('lines drawn'), and repaid first from surplus
revolver_first_variant.rationale: Separates the value of revolver access from the value of optimizing (verify_finance.md H4). This variant pays the undrawn fee.

horizon.rationale: Rolling horizon: each re-solve looks three years ahead from its date with the same rules.

closed_loop.unit: simulate the rolling policy on the tree
closed_loop.rationale: The outcome probabilities of the policy that would actually run: execute the root decision, re-solve at every t = 1 and t = 2 node on a fresh 3-year window from the realized state, execute only its first decision, and settle at t = 3 with the same horizon rows. v1 reported only the static plan's probabilities (verify_finance.md H2).

horizons.rationale: Same parameters and rules with the tree cut at 2, 3 and 4 years; a result that changes with the cut is a horizon effect, not policy.
horizons.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.2 (horizon-invariance test); verify_math.md issue 1; verify_finance.md H1

floors.rationale: Shows what a downside floor would do if the IC set one, instead of building one into the main case: from slack (v1's -3.9% would not bind now that the tail is about -1.7% a year) to tight. The root PE sale is held at zero in every row and priced by a forced re-solve.

value.label: IC lower edge hard everywhere, crisis years included (v1)
Appetite prices 1% (not 2%) for the target and the range
Appetite prices 0.75% for the target and the range
Owner draw 10% in a crisis (Brent below $23)
NAV loan against the whole PE book (v1 capacity)
No terminal burden on unfunded (psi = 0, v1)
PE in crisis leaves at the reported mark (omega = 1, v1)
No price on the 8% cash target (4% floor only, v1)
8% target counted gross of facility draws
Synthetic LEVER of the liquid book allowed
Regimes predict returns (v1 means with post-crisis rebound)

variants.unit: one change at a time from this file; each variant is re-solved with and without the revolver
variants.rationale: The solve is objective, but its answer moves with a handful of human-set inputs. This table names them and their owners (verify_finance.md M9).

action_threshold_bn.rationale: Amounts below $5m are treated as zero in labels and in every P(...) statistic.
action_threshold_bn.source: reporting convention (verify_math.md issue 8: moved here from the script)

binding_tolerance_bn.rationale: An inequality row this close to its bound counts as binding in the report.

tangent_margins.unit: multipliers on the first solve's lowest and highest leaf W/W0
tangent_margins.rationale: Second-pass tangents span slightly more than the first solve's leaf range.

fd_step_bn.rationale: Step for the finite-difference checks of the duals.

kink_probe_bn.rationale: Each decision node's cash price is also measured at +/- $0.5bn of cash; if the two one-sided prices differ by more than kink_rel_tol, the node is flagged as near a kink (verify_finance.md M1).
kink_probe_bn.source: design/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.6 (one-sided derivatives, 'at a kink' label)
